chunks: Such people are asked, “What do you say about the state in which ‘those having a say’ (ahl hal wa aqd) are not able to select an Imam? What is the case of the penalties?” If you say they are not binding, this is abrogation on the same merits you accused us of; and if you say penalties remain enforceable with respect to their deservers; this is our very answer as well.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْحَلِّ وَالْعَقْدِ: Those having a say / those with authority

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hudud during the occultation of the Imam?
ai.summary: Tusi employs a dialectical strategy to resolve the jurisprudential dilemma of applying *hudud* during the Minor and Major Occultation, where the Imam's direct authority is absent. He demonstrates that the opposing school's claim of abrogation contradicts their own premises, while their assertion that penalties remain valid for their rightful recipients inadvertently validates the Shia position of continued divine jurisdiction.
